correctness.rationale: An independent all-direction linearization confirms the coefficient. At step j the centered vertices are λv_i, λ=(−1/3)^j, with v_i·v_i=3/4, v_i·v_l=−1/4 for i≠l, and Σv_iv_iᵀ=I. Write their first variation as D_i=aP+b(v_i·P)v_i. To propagate it, write D_i=T+λFv_i, where T=(a+b/4)P and λF=bΣ(v_l·P)v_lv_lᵀ; to first order the transformed face normal is v_i−Fᵀv_i and the offset is −λ/4+v_i·T. Differentiation of the perpendicular foot gives a′=1−b/12, b′=(4/3)(a−1)+2b/9, so from (0,0) one obtains b at steps 1–4 equal to −4/3, −8/27, 20/243, 112/2187. At step four λ=1/81; the derivative of each normalized edge square is (112/27)(v_i+v_l)·P, since the mean variation vanishes. The six pair sums are exactly the signed Cartesian unit vectors. This proves the all-direction norm and the positive lower bound away from zero locally. The foot map is smooth near these nondegenerate centered iterates.
residual_risks: No maximal local neighborhood or global uniqueness is proved.

For a displacement ℓ toward the apex of altitude H=2/√3, t=(H/4+ℓ)/(3H/4−ℓ), hence dt/dℓ=16/(9H) at zero. Differentiating (1+q)/(3q) at q=1/2 gives −4/3; the lateral/base ratio derivative is therefore 448/(81H)=224√3/81 per unit ℓ.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Three base and three lateral normalized deviations have derivatives ± one half the ratio derivative, so the axial norm coefficient per unit displacement is 112√2/27. The smooth map is equivariant under permutations of the regular tetrahedron's vertices; the standard S₄ representation is irreducible, hence Dg(0)ᵀDg(0) is scalar. That transfers the exact axial coefficient to every direction without further shape information, and Taylor's theorem gives local uniqueness.
